facts.statement: The genus Eosipterus was named in 1997 by paleontologists Ji Shu'an and Ji Qiang.
facts.quote: The genus was named in 1997 by Ji Shu'an and Ji Qiang.

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Eosipterus yangi.
facts.quote: The type species is Eosipterus yangi.

facts.statement: The genus name combines Greek words for 'dawn' and 'wing' with a Latin ending, though a grammar error resulted in the spelling 'Eosipterus' instead of the expected 'Eopterus'.
facts.quote: The genus name is derived from Greek eos, "dawn" and Greek pteron, "wing" with a Latin ending; and a grammar error: normally the combination would have resulted in "eopterus".

facts.statement: The 'dawn' part of the name refers both to the fossil's Early Cretaceous age and to China's location in the east.
facts.quote: The "dawn" element refers to its age but also to China being "in the east".

facts.statement: The specific name 'yangi' honors the paleontologist Yang Daihuan.
facts.quote: The specific name honours paleontologist Yang Daihuan.

facts.statement: Eosipterus was the first pterosaur discovered in the western Liaoning region.
facts.quote: It was the first pterosaur discovered in that region.

facts.statement: Most of the vertebrae in the fossil are severely damaged, making it impossible to determine their exact number.
facts.quote: Most vertebrae have been severely damaged and even their number cannot be determined.

facts.statement: Eighteen detached belly ribs were found in the fossil matrix.
facts.quote: The authors state that eighteen detached belly ribs are present in the matrix.

facts.statement: The wings of Eosipterus are described as robust and elongated.
facts.quote: The wings are robust and elongated.

facts.statement: The wing finger retains the standard four phalanges, unlike the related genus Beipiaopterus which has lost the fourth one.
facts.quote: The wing finger has the standard four phalanges, a difference from the possibly related Beipiaopterus which has lost the fourth phalanx.

facts.statement: The total wingspan of Eosipterus was approximately 1.2 meters.
The femur measures 6 cm in length while the tibia measures 96 mm.
facts.quote: The femur has a length of 6 cm; the tibia of 96 mm.

facts.statement: The fibula is strongly reduced in size.
The foot claws are slightly curved, and the fifth toe is reduced to a single claw.
facts.quote: The foot claws are slightly curved; the fifth toe has been reduced to a single claw.

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Eosipterus date back to the Aptian stage, approximately 125 million years ago.
facts.quote: Fossil remains dated back to the Aptian stage, 125 million years ago.

facts.statement: A 2006 cladistic study identified Eosipterus as a member of the family Ctenochasmatidae, with David Unwin further assigning it to the subfamily Ctenochasmatinae.
facts.quote: A cladistic study in 2006 found that it was a member of the Ctenochasmatidae — David Unwin more precisely assigned it to the Ctenochasmatinae.

facts.statement: The time range for Eosipterus is from the Barremian to the Aptian stages, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)
